title: Ocean food chain cards
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Habitats and blocking sound (Blue Abyss and Can We Block Sound?)
source: Seeded from science/y4 lesson 7 (Ocean food chain cards (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 7: Ocean food chains: producers, predators and prey. To understand how energy passes along an ocean food chain from producers to predators

cards:
producer
a living thing that makes its
own food using sunlight

consumer
a living thing that eats
others for food

predator
an animal that hunts others

prey
an animal that is hunted

food chain
shows what eats what, with
arrows
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Order these into a chain: shark, plankton, small fish.
questions.model: Find the producer first: plankton. Who eats plankton? Small fish. Who eats small fish? The shark. Arrows point to the eater.

questions.q: In 'krill → whale', which is the predator?
Where does the energy in every food chain start?
Make two ocean food chains from the cards and label producer, consumer, predator and prey.
questions.a: For example: plankton → krill → whale; seaweed → crab → octopus → seal, correctly labelled
questions.model: Teacher builds the first chain on screen: 'plankton (producer) → krill (prey) → whale (predator)'.

questions.q: Which animal in your chains is both predator and prey? Explain.
questions.a: For example: the octopus eats crabs and is eaten by seals

questions.q: Why are there always more plankton than sharks?
questions.a: Energy is lost at each step, so less food reaches the top; fewer animals can be fed there

questions.q: Big question: why do the tiniest living things matter to whales?
questions.a: Plankton start the food chain: krill eat them and whales eat krill.
